# Miller's Book Review

> > A literary criticism and book review site exploring classic and contemporary literature, publishing culture, and the enduring power of books in shaping ideas and society.

Miller's Book Review features essays, interviews, and critical analysis by Joel J Miller examining canonical literature, publishing history, and cultural commentary. The site emphasizes literary criticism, author interviews, and thoughtful reflection on books' role in intellectual and social life.

## Key Topics

- Joel J Miller
- Literary criticism
- Book review
- Publishing history
- Cormac McCarthy
- C.S. Lewis
- Gothic fiction
- Author interviews
- Cultural history
- Literary analysis
- Classic literature
- 1990s culture
- Editorial processes
- Authenticity critique
- Intellectual freedom

## Literary Essays & Reviews

- [Just Like Yourself, Perhaps](https://www.millersbookreview.com/p/cormac-mccarthy-child-of-god): Review of Cormac McCarthy's gothic novel 'Child of God' and its Appalachian setting.
- [How Stories Work, Especially the Spooky Ones](https://www.millersbookreview.com/p/henry-james-the-turn-of-the-screw): Review of Henry James's 'The Turn of the Screw' exploring gothic fiction and narrative ambiguity.
- [The Devil Went down to Moscow](https://www.millersbookreview.com/p/bulgakov-master-and-margarita): Review of Mikhail Bulgakov's Soviet classic 'The Master and Margarita' and its satire.
- [Unraveling Narnia's Genetic Code](https://www.millersbookreview.com/p/c-s-lewis-narnia-warwick-ball-east-of-wardrobe): Review of Warwick Ball's 'East of the Wardrobe' analyzing C.S. Lewis's creative sources.

## Ideas, Culture & Intellectual Freedom

- [Books Divide Us, but They Can Also Heal](https://www.millersbookreview.com/p/books-divide-us-but-they-can-also-heal): Essay on book censorship, literary freedom, and responses to controversial content with Margaret Atwood.
- [The Education of Malcolm X](https://www.millersbookreview.com/p/education-of-malcolm-x): Essay on Malcolm X's self-education through books while imprisoned, examining literacy and race.
- [Not Useless: We Just Don't Know What It's for Yet](https://www.millersbookreview.com/p/flexner-useless-knowledge): Review of Abraham Flexner's essay on useless knowledge and fundamental research innovation.
- [The Cult of Authenticity: Life in the 1990s](https://www.millersbookreview.com/p/chuck-klosterman-nineties-cult-of-authenticity): Review of Chuck Klosterman's 'The Nineties' examining 1990s culture, grunge, and authenticity.
- [Culture Is What We Make It—All of Us](https://www.millersbookreview.com/p/martin-puchner-culture-is-what-we-make-it): Interview with Harvard's Martin Puchner on 'Culture: The Story of Us, From Cave Art to K-Pop'.
- [Why We're Still Obsessed with Dead Greeks](https://www.millersbookreview.com/p/nadya-williams-why-were-still-obsessed-with-dead-greeks): Interview with Nadya Williams on classics literature, cultural decline, and ancient philosophy.

## Publishing & Literary Craft

- [3 Literary Deaths and the Ever-Evolving Book Business](https://www.millersbookreview.com/p/3-literary-deaths-mccarthy-gottlieb-snyder): Reflections on deaths of Cormac McCarthy, Robert Gottlieb, and Richard Snyder's publishing legacy.
- [First Thing We Do, Let's Kill All the Copy Editors?*](https://www.millersbookreview.com/p/nassim-nicholas-taleb-copy-editors): Essay on editorial processes, copy editing, and author-editor relationships with Nassim Taleb.
- [The Bookcase as World's Most Underrated UI](https://www.millersbookreview.com/p/bookcase-worlds-most-underrated-ui): Analysis of print books vs. ebooks, examining why physical books dominate despite digital alternatives.
- [Bookish Diversions: Type-Oh, Dang It!](https://www.millersbookreview.com/p/bookish-diversions-type-oh-dangit): Essay on typos in James Joyce, the Bible, and publishing history's curious errors.

## Author Interviews & Conversations

- ['Love Triumphs over Violence—Eventually'](https://www.millersbookreview.com/p/cynthia-l-haven-rene-girard-joy-davidman): Interview with Cynthia L. Haven on René Girard, Joy Davidman, and literary criticism.
- [Wrestling Coach Bets on Tolstoy and Dante to Save the Classics—and Young Men](https://www.millersbookreview.com/p/joshua-d-phillips-wrestling-coach-bets-on-tolstoy-and-dante-to-save-the-classics-and-young-men): Interview with Joshua D. Phillips on using classic literature to engage young male readers.
- [No Silos: The Challenge of Finding Your Audience](https://www.millersbookreview.com/p/john-j-thompson-finding-your-audience): Interview with John J. Thompson on indie publishing, alternative media, and audience building.

## Reader Community & Open Threads

- [Open Thread: One Author You're Grateful For?](https://www.millersbookreview.com/p/one-author-youre-grateful-for): Reader discussion prompt on favorite authors including Mencken, Lewis, Chesterton, and Eliot.
- [Open Thread: Authors You've Read Most?](https://www.millersbookreview.com/p/open-thread-authors-youve-read-most): Reader discussion on frequently-read authors and personal reading habits across fiction/nonfiction.
